title: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 — Section 3 (Receipt of written communications)

content.overview: Section 3 governs receipt of written communications in arbitral proceedings, subject to party agreement and with an express exclusion for communications concerning judicial-authority proceedings.
content.glance: Unless otherwise agreed: personal/designated-address delivery, or after reasonable inquiry a last-known-address route with a delivery record; judicial communications excluded.
content.study: Section 3(1) is subject to contrary party agreement. Ordinary delivery is personal or at place of business, habitual residence or mailing address. Section 3(1)(b) permits a last-known-address route after reasonable inquiry. Section 3(2) deems receipt on the day of delivery. Section 3(3) excludes judicial-authority communications.

sections.heading: Default subject to agreement
sections.body: Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, the statutory delivery routes apply.

sections.heading: Ordinary delivery
sections.body: Personal delivery or delivery at the addressee's place of business, habitual residence or mailing address.

sections.heading: Last-known-address route
sections.body: If those places cannot be found after reasonable inquiry, send to the last known address by registered letter or another means providing a record of the attempt.

sections.heading: Deemed date and exclusion
sections.body: Deemed receipt is the day of delivery. Communications concerning judicial-authority proceedings are excluded.

examples.title: Personal delivery
examples.body: Notice delivered personally during the arbitral process is received on the day of delivery, subject to any agreed method.

examples.title: Last-known-address
examples.body: After reasonable inquiry fails to locate current addresses, a registered letter to the last known mailing address may engage s. 3(1)(b).

hypotheticals.question: Can last-known-address delivery skip reasonable inquiry?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 3(1)(b) requires that the specified places cannot be found after reasonable inquiry.

rows.right: Places not found after reasonable inquiry

misconceptions.trap: Any letter to a last known address is automatically deemed received.
misconceptions.correction: Reasonable inquiry and the statutory delivery method are required.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What must be established for deemed receipt under section 3?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Identify the communication, check any agreed method, establish the applicable delivery route, prove the delivery record and, for s. 3(1)(b), the required reasonable inquiry.

enhancement.definition: Section 3 governs receipt of written communications in arbitral proceedings.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Agreed method, or statutory delivery routes with deemed receipt on delivery day; judicial communications excluded.
